title: Forge effect provenance v1 (an additive payload extension at event_schema 1)
description: The optional, absent-by-default payload fields decision 0016 adds to effect/started and effect/failed. They are legal at event_schema 1 under the amended rule in contracts/README.md: they are optional, absent by default, published here as a numbered extension schema, and never read by fold — the engine derives the next chain index by scanning the effect's own events, exactly as it already scans them for the last error, and RunState gains nothing. A v1 consumer that ignores these fields folds to the identical state.

provenance.description: Present on effect/started ONLY when at least one invocation site of this seat is agent-resolved. A LIST keyed by invocation site, because provenance is per driver INVOCATION and not per attempt: a panel runs N members inside one attempt, and a sequence may span two providers. Hanging one model beside the attempt would print a false statement in every readout.

member.description: The invocation-site tag the engine already uses for checkpoints: null for a single seat, '<member>' for a panel member, '<step>' for a sequence step, '<step>:<member>' for a member inside a step panel.

chain_index.description: Which link of the agent's chain this invocation used. Greater than zero means a bounded fallback happened, and every readout says so — the forge never claims the second choice equals the first.

start_failure.description: Present on effect/failed only when the STRUCTURAL fail-to-start predicate held for at least one invocation site: Failed, and no Accepted ever received, and no checkpoint emitted. No stderr sniffing and no 'model not found' regex — the engine never pattern-matches a provider's prose to make a control decision. Once Accepted arrives, fallback is unreachable by construction, which is decision 0016's mid-session boundary mechanised rather than described.

start_failure_sites.description: Which invocation sites failed to start, in declared order, tagged exactly as provenance[].member. This is what the per-site chain index folds over: in a panel, a member that failed to start advances its own chain index and a member that ran does not.
